<!--
A figure built out of sub-figures is laid out by quarto itself, in the grid
that layout-ncol asks for. apafloatlatex.lua used to take such a float over
and wrap it in a figure environment by hand as soon as any panel carried an
apa-note, which replaced the float with a plain div and cost it that grid:
the panels came out stacked one per row.

Render from the tests directory:

    quarto render subfigure-layout-grid.qmd

A successful run produces a PDF in which

  - every layout below is two panels wide, not one;
  - each note appears exactly once, under the panel it belongs to, or under
    the whole grid when it belongs to the figure;
  - every figure is numbered and every reference resolves (no "Figure ??"),
    including the layouts that have no caption text of their own.

In the .tex, each of the five layouts should carry two \begin{minipage}
wrappers, and every float a \caption with a \label.
-->

# Cases

A: captioned layout, no notes (@fig-a).

::: {#fig-a layout-ncol=2}
![Left.](sampleimage.png){#fig-a-1 width="1.5in"}

![Right.](sampleimage.png){#fig-a-2 width="1.5in"}

An overall caption.
:::

B: caption-less layout, no notes (@fig-b). Quarto writes no `\caption` for a
laid-out float whose caption is empty, and the `\label` goes with it, so this
one used to render unnumbered with a dangling reference.

::: {#fig-b layout-ncol=2}
![Left.](sampleimage.png){#fig-b-1 width="1.5in"}

![Right.](sampleimage.png){#fig-b-2 width="1.5in"}
:::

C: captioned layout, both panels noted (@fig-c).

::: {#fig-c layout-ncol=2}
![Left.](sampleimage.png){#fig-c-1 width="1.5in" apa-note="Note for the left panel."}

![Right.](sampleimage.png){#fig-c-2 width="1.5in" apa-note="Note for the right panel."}

An overall caption.
:::

D: caption-less layout, both panels noted (@fig-d). The case from issue #158,
and the one that has to keep both the grid and its number.

::: {#fig-d layout-ncol=2}
![Left.](sampleimage.png){#fig-d-1 width="1.5in" apa-note="Note for the left panel."}

![Right.](sampleimage.png){#fig-d-2 width="1.5in" apa-note="Note for the right panel."}
:::

E: layout with a note on the whole figure rather than on the panels
(@fig-e). The note belongs to the figure, so it is printed once, below the
grid, and not copied onto each panel.

::: {#fig-e layout-ncol=2 apa-note="A note belonging to the whole figure."}
![Left.](sampleimage.png){#fig-e-1 width="1.5in"}

![Right.](sampleimage.png){#fig-e-2 width="1.5in"}

An overall caption.
:::

H: layout with a whole-figure note and no layout attribute at all (@fig-h).

::: {#fig-h apa-note="A note belonging to the whole figure."}
![Left.](sampleimage.png){#fig-h-1 width="1.5in"}

![Right.](sampleimage.png){#fig-h-2 width="1.5in"}

An overall caption.
:::

I: three panels over two columns, with a whole-figure note (@fig-i).

::: {#fig-i layout-ncol=2 apa-note="A note belonging to the whole three-panel figure, long enough to show whether it wraps inside half the figure width or runs the full width of it."}
![One.](sampleimage.png){#fig-i-1 width="1.2in"}

![Two.](sampleimage.png){#fig-i-2 width="1.2in"}

![Three.](sampleimage.png){#fig-i-3 width="1.2in"}

An overall caption.
:::

J: explicit layout matrix with a whole-figure note (@fig-j).

::: {#fig-j layout="[[1,1]]" apa-note="A note belonging to the whole figure."}
![Left.](sampleimage.png){#fig-j-1 width="1.5in"}

![Right.](sampleimage.png){#fig-j-2 width="1.5in"}

An overall caption.
:::

F: plain single figure with a note (@fig-f). Not a layout; it still takes the
hand-built wrapper.

![A single image.](sampleimage.png){#fig-f width="1.5in" apa-note="A single figure's note."}

G: plain single figure, no note, no caption text (@fig-g).
